usage: Recent form rankings. Each player is ranked on the average actual fantasy points of that player's own last three completed games, under this league's exact scoring. The three games are the three highest scoring periods for which ESPN reported an actual score for that player, so two players in the same table can be using different weeks after a bye. A game qualifies only when the player actually appeared in it: ESPN must have reported an actual entry (statSourceId 0) for that scoring period AND that entry must carry the games-played marker (stat 210). The presence of a scoring row alone is not enough, because ESPN also emits 0.0 rows for players who did not play, and counting those would understate recent form. A game the player did appear in counts even when it scored 0.00 - a receiver targeted with no catch, a quarterback with one incomplete pass - and diagnostics.zero_point_games_kept reports how many such real appearances were kept, while diagnostics.not_played_excluded reports how many did-not-play rows were discarded. A bye or a missed game simply does not count. A player with fewer than three qualifying games is excluded entirely; nothing is padded and no placeholder row exists. Weekly points come from ESPN's appliedTotal on a league-scoped request, which already applies this league's scoring settings; scoring_crosscheck independently recomputes them from league.json scoring_settings and reports the largest disagreement. Lists are sorted by avg_3_game_exact descending with ties broken by ascending ESPN player id; avg_3_game_display carries the two decimals to show. owner_label is the owning fantasy team's current name, or FREE AGENT, or WAIVERS, or UNKNOWN when the id is absent from player_index.json, resolved by ESPN player id only. is_jason_x is true only when that index reports fantasy_status ROSTERED and fantasy_team_id equal to ownership.jason_x_team_id, regardless of starter, bench or IR slot, and it is what drives the pale-yellow row highlight in the daily PDF: highlight every row where it is true and no other row. The team id is the authority rather than the team name because teams in this league get renamed mid-season; ownership.jason_x_team_name_observed is the name that id currently carries, and ownership.jason_x_name_id_agree is false when the name no longer selects the same players as the id. Because a game counts once the player has appeared in it, a snapshot taken while games are in progress can count a partially played week for players whose game has already kicked off; weeks.with_data shows which periods contributed.

scoring_crosscheck.note: ESPN appliedTotal is authoritative and is the value ranked. This block recomputes sum(stats[statId] * scoringItems[statId].points), honouring pointsOverrides by defaultPositionId, purely so silent scoring drift is detectable. It never changes a ranking.

ownership.source: player_index.json players_by_id from this same snapshot run
ownership.match: ESPN player id only; no name matching
